answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with adaptive cross-examination panels. Before an identity gains paid work, three random peers probe its claimed history in real time, asking follow-ups no script can predict. Like light through a prism, one claim splits into many angles, and inconsistencies show at once. Passing earns a velvet pass to the paid tier; failure marks the identity and its sponsors. A saffron fee funds the panel, refunded only on a pass. Faking a hundred identities means staffing a hundred live defences at once, costing far more than the work is worth.
